title: Positivity of the Composed Running Time
statement: Let $C_1$ be a contract for $M$ from entry state $e_1$ to the singleton exit state $e_2$, and let $C_2$ be a contract for $M$ from $e_2$ to exit set $X$. Let $\mathrm{link}$ map parameters of $C_1$ to parameters of $C_2$. Suppose every endpoint of $C_1$ from an admissible start satisfies the corresponding linked precondition of $C_2$, and before the end of the first run the state is outside $X$. If $C_1$ has strictly positive prescribed running time for every admissible start, then the contract obtained by composing $C_1$ and $C_2$ has strictly positive prescribed running time for every admissible start.
hypotheses_covered: $C_1$ is a contract for $M$ from $e_1$ to $\{e_2\}$
$C_2$ is a contract for $M$ from $e_2$ to $X$
Every admissible $C_1$ endpoint satisfies the linked $C_2$ precondition
Before the $C_1$ running time, the run's state is outside $X$
$C_1$ has positive running time on every admissible start
replaced:
Let $C_1$ and $C_2$ be contracts for the same multi-tape Turing machine, where $C_1$
enters at $e_1$ and exits at $e_2$, and $C_2$ enters at $e_2$ and exits in a set $X$.
Let $\mathrm{link}$ map parameters of $C_1$ to parameters of $C_2$. Assume each endpoint
of $C_1$ satisfies the precondition of $C_2$ at the linked parameter, and that before
the $C_1$ running time the machine's state never belongs to $X$. If $C_1$ has strictly
positive running time for every admissible starting configuration, then the contract
formed by sequentially composing $C_1$ and $C_2$ also has strictly positive running time
for every admissible starting configuration.
